name: Elliott
label: Revelation
lede: Louisville hardcore kids who traded breakdowns for pianos, samplers and a string section, broke up the year their best record came out, and waited nineteen years to play it again.

eras.title: Out of Louisville hardcore
eras.text: Chris Higdon, Jonathan Mobley and Jay Palumbo came from the Louisville hardcore bands Falling Forward and Empathy, and set out on purpose to sound like neither. The models were Quicksand, Jawbox and Sunny Day Real Estate; the result landed them on Revelation.

years.h: Elliott form in Louisville from Falling Forward and Empathy
years.p: Guitarist Jay Palumbo joins singer-guitarist Chris Higdon and bassist Jonathan Mobley, with Ben Lord on drums. Revelation's bio calls the aim melodic hardcore, rock and emo in one band.

years.h: Kevin Ratterman replaces Ben Lord on drums
years.p: Kevin Ratterman takes over from Ben Lord. He becomes the one member besides Chris Higdon in Elliott from here to the end, and the one who drags in samplers and ambient sounds.
Two songs, with Ben Lord on drums. The phrase sticks: Elliott's Bandcamp is elliottintransit, and their documentary is called In Transition.

Elliott's full-length debut on Revelation: big crooning melodies over post-hardcore guitars. Chris Higdon lists [[Jawbreaker|ec88cdc3-0517-4951-b5ef-7323e7316db0]], [[Seaweed|82aa1374-7c47-43e8-857d-11d723fe4c1a]], [[Sugar|e3347fbd-2595-480e-926d-278566debf9d]] and [[Foo Fighters|67f66c07-6e61-4026-ade5-7e782fad3a5d]] among the touchstones.

eras.title: Pianos, drum machines and a tour gone wrong
eras.text: False Cathedrals made Elliott a name well beyond Kentucky, and nearly broke the band making it. Two founders were gone soon after, and a slot opening for the Toadies ended halfway through.

years.p: If They Do goes darker and heavier. Will You has an early Calvary Song and a cover of [[The Chameleons|8d07f60f-b9f4-46c0-9c27-31de0fb9b671]].

q: Making that record was intense, the schedule and the pressure we put on ourselves.
years.src: Revelation Records · The Pitch of Discontent
years.p: Kevin Ratterman adds samplers and drum machines; Chris Higdon adds harmonies and piano. A Punknews reviewer later called it the most beautiful music he'd heard in his life.

years.h: Jay Palumbo and Jonathan Mobley step away from Elliott
years.p: Palumbo leaves over creative differences and Mobley cuts back. Benny Clark of Falling Forward joins on guitar and Jason Skaggs on bass. Palumbo's next band is [[Thirty-Two Frames|9a47ec35-e682-4350-800e-d26981a86d10]].

years.src: The Pitch of Discontent · This Was The Scene
years.h: Elliott get dropped halfway through a Toadies tour
years.p: Elliott were opening for [[Toadies|066e598e-baa0-4e34-b511-c70bcec6f783]] in 2001 when they were pulled off midway, over what the band called disagreement with management decisions.
years.xp: Chris Higdon talks through the Toadies tour on the This Was The Scene podcast, episode 170, along with how differently the band played False Cathedrals live compared with the record.

years.h: Elliott play Furnace Fest in Alabama
years.p: Elliott play the 2002 edition of Furnace Fest. Twenty years later, the same festival brings them back.

eras.title: The best record, then the end
eras.text: Elliott's third album started as an EP and grew into their most ambitious record, with strings from fellow Louisvillians Rachel's. The band announced it was finishing before most fans had heard it.

years.h: Song in the Air, with strings by Rachel's
years.p: Self-produced, 49 minutes, with the seven-minute Beijing (Too Many People). Pitchfork called it more dynamic and cohesive than anything Elliott had done before.

years.h: Elliott say goodbye across Europe and North America
years.p: After announcing the end, Elliott play farewell tours of Europe and North America and break up in November 2003, seven months after Song in the Air.

eras.title: In transit
eras.text: The breakup left behind a live record, a film and a compilation. The members scattered into other work: Chris Higdon fronted Frontier(s), and Kevin Ratterman built a recording studio in a funeral home.

years.p: Live-in-the-studio recordings and outtakes from Elliott's last days on CD, packaged with a DVD that includes the documentary In Transition: A Film About Elliott.
Another look back at Elliott's catalog, ten years after the breakup. Meanwhile Kevin Ratterman runs his Louisville studio, The Funeral Home.

eras.title: Nineteen years, then Furnace Fest
eras.text: Elliott came back on the stage where they'd played in 2002, with Jay Palumbo back on guitar and a new bassist. Then Chris Higdon started something new.

years.h: Elliott reunite for Furnace Fest, their first show in 19 years
years.p: Announced in February 2022: Chris Higdon, Kevin Ratterman and original guitarist Jay Palumbo, with Ashli State on bass. Elliott have stayed active since.

years.h: False Cathedrals reunion show, Warsaw, Brooklyn, 2022
yt: False Cathedrals reunion show, Warsaw, Brooklyn, 2022

years.h: Chris Higdon's new band [[Mirrorless|25139c5f-877b-4dec-9e46-a010442dd27b]] debuts on Equal Vision
years.p: A six-song melodic hardcore EP with Ryan Patterson of [[Coliseum|7f43923c-31d0-4c8f-9708-1779adf4b3a9]], Brian Roundtree of [[By the Grace of God|42a5a24f-7fa9-4790-879d-fe5fb3d91f9f]] and drummer Ben Sears.
